THE RESULT: a client holding a genuine signed tree head, running the consistency check, PASSING IT CORRECTLY, and silently installing a backdoored module — because the fork was one record BEYOND the head it held. A cached head buys detection at or below its own size and nothing past it, and afterwards the client's single-slot memory has been overwritten with the attacker's branch, so it cannot notice later either. Also measured: sum.golang.org's checkpoint carries exactly ONE signature line, its own; there is no /checkpoint endpoint; 'gossip' appears ZERO times in all of go1.24.7's cmd/go; and the client is built with a single-verifier list, so a witness cosignature would land in UnverifiedSigs and be ignored. The note format supports N signers. The deployment uses one.

BE CAREFUL HOW YOU REPEAT THAT. It is NOT a live break of Go: it presupposes the signing key or a hostile GOSUMDB, and under key compromise a transparency log is designed to leave evidence rather than to prevent. Overstating it is the e000010 error and I would rather you undersold it.
